title: GPT-assisted proof reduces Zieve’s Hurwitz realizability conjecture to the three-branch-point case
summary: The authors prove that, assuming Zieve-admissible branch data are realizable for three branch points, all such data with four or more branch points are realizable. This establishes that no additional obstruction arises solely from adding branch points; the underlying three-branch-point conjecture remains open. The paper discloses GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra assistance in exploring reduction strategies and in proof development and checking.
ai_technology: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra
organization: School of Mathematical Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China; National Engineering Laboratory for Brain-inspired Intelligence Technology and Applications, University of Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: The authors prove that, assuming Zieve-admissible branch data are realizable for three branch points, all such data with four or more branch points are realizable.
evidence.unknown: This is a new conditional mathematical reduction theorem, not a resolution of Zieve’s full conjecture: the three-branch-point case remains open. The source is an arXiv preprint; human authors report reviewing AI-assisted work and accept responsibility, but no independent verification of the proof is claimed here.
evidence.ai_role: Authors explicitly report that the models assisted throughout the research, including exploration of reduction strategies and proof development/checking, as well as notation consistency and manuscript work. Humans reviewed all AI-assisted content and take responsibility for the proof.
